marta: quick note — ran into a weird mypy/pyright mismatch with autogenerated client models in the python SDK. the generator turns Optional[Sequence[str]] into Sequence[Optional[Any]] in the emitted stub, so element typing is lost.

owen: ouch. any minimal repro?

marta: yes, pasted small example from examples/sampleapp: 
```py
# generated stub snippet (bad)
class Row(BaseModel):
    tags: Sequence[Optional[Any]]

# expected
class Row(BaseModel):
    tags: Optional[Sequence[str]]

# consequence: callers doing `row.tags[0].upper()` fail static-checks because element type is Any/Optional[Any] and mypy complains about attribute access.
```

li: that sounds like two bugs in one: (1) union/optional normalization flattening and converting to Any, (2) we don't emit types in .pyi consistent with runtime model due to lack of forward refs. do we include `from __future__ import annotations` in generated modules?

marta: not currently, which makes runtime and stub semantics diverge. also noticed the generator sometimes rewrites Sequence -> List which trips some downstream code expecting typing.Sequence.

build-bot: created issue SDK-7823 with failing sampleapp CI logs and mypy output. CI link: https://ci.redwood/test/7823 :rotating_light:

owen: proposed quick fixes: preserve Optional wrapper during normalization, avoid collapsing generics when origin matches but args differ, and add pyi output that mirrors runtime stubs. also add a small static-checker smoke in the SDK CI that runs both mypy and pyright against examples/.

li: i can send a draft for the generator change. also suggest adding a regression test: generate code, write a tiny consumer that accesses element methods (like .upper), and run mypy expecting no errors. cheap and catches this class of bugs.

marta: sounds good. for immediate onboarding relief we can update sampleapp docs suggesting `# type: ignore[call-arg]` or using typing.cast to the expected Sequence[str] at call site — not ideal but lowers support tickets.

sam: bumping priority — customer hit during POC. if PR lands we should cut a patch release for the pip package and tag it in the Hosted SDK docs.

li: will open draft PR and @sam. i'll include pyi generation and add `from __future__ import annotations` to the top of generated modules.

nowen: also note pyright's stricter handling of Optional in containers — adding pyright to CI is valuable.

marta: thanks everyone. leaving the sampleapp repro under examples/onboarding/typing-repro. will post the PR link here when ready.

sam: ping me on the PR; i can help with release notes and patch cut. :thumbsup:
